summary: Audit log export missing Optimization Config rollback event (Console/API rollback succeeds, no event in SIEM feed)
description:
Issue summary
Northbridge Analytics reports that Optimization Config rollback actions are not appearing in their audit log export / SIEM pipeline. Rollback itself succeeds (traffic returns to baseline), and they can see other Optimization Config lifecycle events (create/apply/promote) in the audit feed.

Impact
- Customer compliance/change-management requirement: all production rollbacks must be auditable with actor + scope + before/after.
- Procurement blocker for enabling Safe Apply + Rollback broadly across their org.
- No production outage, but compliance risk + inability to prove rollback action occurred.

Customer report
- They rolled back Optimization Config via Console (Rollback button) on 2026-02-11 ~18:40 UTC.
- They expected an audit event within ~1–2 minutes in their exported audit stream.
- They can correlate the rollback in Redwood Console history and via performance recovery, but there is no corresponding audit event in their feed.

Expected behavior
Audit event should be emitted and exported for rollback actions (Console + API) with:
- event_name matching taxonomy
- actor identity (user_id/email or service principal)
- request_id/correlation_id
- scope (tenant/model/region)
- config_version_from + config_version_to
- outcome (success/failure)

Actual behavior
Rollback event not present in exported audit feed. Apply/promote events show up as expected.

Environment
- Deployment mode: Dedicated (customer)
- Region: us-east
- Affected feature: Optimization Config rollback

Notes / attachments
- Customer provided: rollback timestamp, affected tenant slug, and SIEM query screenshots (not attached here). Support has them in the customer thread.

Initial triage checklist
- Confirm rollback happened in Console history and in control-plane event logs.
- Verify whether event was emitted but dropped by exporter (schema mismatch / missing required fields).
- Verify taxonomy match vs documented event names in Confluence.
- Confirm whether rollback endpoint path uses the same audit emitter as apply/promote.

Internal references
- Audit event taxonomy: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/optimization-config-audit-events.json
- Rollback endpoint PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-19902-add-rollback-endpoint.json
- Audit events PR: sources/github/redwood/pr-19941-add-audit-log-events-for-config-changes.json
comments:
2026-02-12 09:18 UTC — Kevin Osei (Reporter)
Customer escalation from Northbridge Analytics: rollback action does not appear in audit log export. They can see optimization_config.apply + optimization_config.promote events, but not rollback. Marking as P1 due to enterprise compliance blocker.

2026-02-12 10:02 UTC — Benji Okafor (Assignee)
Reproduced in staging with SIEM-export mode enabled. Rollback succeeds, history updates, but exporter shows 0 rollback events. Control-plane internal logs show an event emitted with name "optimization_config.rollback".

2026-02-12 10:27 UTC — Marcus Lin (Security)
The documented taxonomy page expects event_name "optimization_config.rolled_back" (past tense) with required field "action" and "result". If emitted name differs, exporter filter will drop. Please confirm exporter allowlist.

2026-02-12 11:05 UTC — Benji Okafor
Confirmed: audit-exporter allowlist includes "optimization_config.rolled_back" but not "optimization_config.rollback". The rollback endpoint is emitting the non-allowlisted name. Apply/promote code paths use the correct names.

2026-02-12 11:22 UTC — Jordan Lee
Also noticed rollback endpoint payload omits "previous_config_version" (it only includes target_version). Exporter schema validation requires both for optimization config changes, otherwise it drops the event.

2026-02-12 12:10 UTC — Benji Okafor
Fix plan:
1) Update rollback endpoint audit event name to taxonomy-compliant "optimization_config.rolled_back".
2) Include required fields: previous_config_version, new_config_version, scope.
3) Add integration test asserting exporter receives rollback events.

2026-02-13 16:44 UTC — Benji Okafor
Opened fix PR and requested review from Security + Console.

2026-02-14 09:30 UTC — Dr. Aisha Rahman
Approved taxonomy alignment. Please ensure request_id is always present and actor identity is captured for both Console and API rollbacks.

2026-02-17 14:12 UTC — Hannah Rivera (Console)
Verified Console rollback uses same endpoint; once backend emits corrected event, Console should be fine. Also asked to add UI note: audit event may be delayed by export pipeline.

2026-02-18 18:06 UTC — Benji Okafor
Fix merged and rolled to prod-us-east. Confirmed in internal SIEM test tenant: rollback generates event within 60–90s.

2026-02-19 15:40 UTC — Kevin Osei
Follow-up with Northbridge: asked them to re-run rollback in a low-risk scope and confirm event appears in their feed. Offered to provide sample payload and correlation_id for their query.

2026-02-20 10:05 UTC — Kevin Osei
Customer confirmed rollback event now appears with expected fields. Closing ticket.
resolution: Root cause: rollback endpoint emitted a non-taxonomy event name ("optimization_config.rollback") and omitted required schema fields, causing the audit-export pipeline allowlist/schema validation to drop the event. Fix: updated rollback audit emission to taxonomy-compliant event name ("optimization_config.rolled_back"), added required version-diff fields + request_id + actor, and added integration coverage to prevent regression. Deployed to prod us-east; customer verified audit feed includes rollback events.
customer_visible_update: We identified an issue where rollback actions were not being included in exported audit logs due to an internal event taxonomy mismatch. The rollback operation itself was successful, but the audit record was filtered out during export. We deployed a fix so rollback actions now generate the expected audit log event with the required fields. Please re-test and let us know if any additional fields are needed for your SIEM queries.
